subject.title: fix(perf): gateway startup benchmark reports n/a CPU/RSS on Windows

question: Should the Windows startup benchmark add an exact child-side CPU snapshot at readiness, or should it continue to omit CPU gating on Windows until that boundary can be measured accurately?
rationale: The PR’s external CIM design can obtain real CPU values, but it cannot guarantee that the value corresponds to the existing ready-boundary definition of startup CPU without changing the benchmark/runtime measurement contract.

options.title: Add a ready-boundary CPU snapshot
options.body: Emit or expose the child process CPU total at the same point it signals readiness, then derive Windows startup CPU from that value.

options.title: Keep Windows CPU unavailable for now
options.body: Land only an accurately scoped RSS capability later and retain `cpu=n/a` on Windows until a boundary-correct CPU measurement exists.

recommendation.title: Add a ready-boundary CPU snapshot
recommendation.body: Emit or expose the child process CPU total at the same point it signals readiness, then derive Windows startup CPU from that value.

likelyOwner.reason: No reliable current-main ownership provenance could be read in this review environment.
